<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The domestic production deduction was repealed by TCJA.&nbsp;&nbsp;Share-based payment compensation represents the impact of applying ASU 2016-09, which requires recognition immediately in the tax provision of certain effects of share-based payments that were possibly deferred under the previous guidance.&nbsp;&nbsp;Tax reform and changes in tax laws represents the impact of TCJA, New Jersey tax reform enacted in 2018, and other enacted tax rate changes.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s accounting for TCJA&#8217;s one-time toll charge on previously undistributed accumulated foreign earnings was completed in the third quarter of 2018, resulting in a $2,105 measurement period tax benefit and corresponding reduction in taxes payable.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has determined that it will elect an accounting policy to treat tax on global low-taxed income (&#8220;GILTI&#8221;) inclusions under TCJA as a period cost when incurred.</p>

<p style="text-align:right;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(4,608</p></td>
<td valign="bottom"  BGCOLOR="#CFF0FC" style="padding-left:0pt;padding-Right:0.75pt;padding-Top:0.75pt;width:1%; border-bottom:double 2.5pt transparent;white-space:nowrap;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:0pt;;text-indent:0pt;;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">)</p></td>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;letter-spacing:0pt;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company expects to maintain a domestic valuation allowance against state NOLs and state credits tax due to restrictive rules regarding realization and recent history of state losses.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company expects to maintain a valuation allowance against certain foreign deferred tax assets, primarily NOL carryforwards, until such time as the Company attains an appropriate level of future profitability in the appropriate jurisdictions and is able to conclude that it is more likely than not that its foreign deferred tax assets are realizable.&#160;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;letter-spacing:0pt;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In July 2018, New Jersey enacted comprehensive corporate income tax reform legislation which included, among other items, the imposition of a multi-year temporary surtax, mandatory combined reporting starting in 2019, revised NOL and dividend exclusion rules, and decoupling from certain federal tax reform provisions.&nbsp;&nbsp;In October 2018 New Jersey enacted additional tax legislation that included significant technical corrections and clarifications to the July law as well as other substantive changes to the State&#8217;s corporate tax regime, and in December 2018 and January 2019 New Jersey issued technical guidance on combined reporting and New Jersey&#8217;s treatment of certain TCJA items such as GILTI income and related GILTI and foreign-derived income (&#8220;FDII&#8221;) special tax deductions, as well as the sourcing of GILTI and FDII, which were considerably different than the July 2018 tax reform law.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;letter-spacing:0pt;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the third quarter of 2018, under New Jersey&#8217;s July 2018 tax reform law as enacted, the Company recorded a discrete benefit of $11,437 to release valuation allowance against New Jersey NOLs and state net deferred tax assets against which the Company had previously maintained a full valuation allowance. The determination to release the valuation allowance was based on the impact and sourcing in future combined reporting of GILTI income without the related GILTI and FDII special deductions, which would have allowed the Company to use the entire New Jersey NOL before expiration. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">62</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CAMBREX CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(dollars in thousands, except share and per share data)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;letter-spacing:0pt;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU62"></a><font style="letter-spacing:0pt;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company considers both positive and negative evidence related to the likelihood of realization of deferred tax asset</font><font style="letter-spacing:0pt;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">s. If, based on the weight of available evidence, it is more likely than not the deferred tax assets will not be realized, the Company records a valuation allowance against all or a portion of the deferred tax assets to adjust the balance to the amount con</font><font style="letter-spacing:0pt;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">sidered more likely than not to be realized. The weight given to the positive and negative evidence is commensurate with the extent to which the evidence may be objectively verified.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;letter-spacing:0pt;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">This assessment, which is completed on a taxing jurisdiction basis, takes into account a number of types of evidence, including the nature, frequency, and severity of current and cumulative financial reporting losses, sources of future taxable income, future reversals of existing taxable temporary differences, and prudent and feasible tax planning strategies, weighted by objectivity.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;letter-spacing:0pt;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In the fourth quarter of 2018, the enactment of New Jersey&#8217;s October 2018 tax reform law and related guidance, which allows GILTI and FDII special tax deductions, and notably provides a separate apportionment methodology for sourcing net GILTI income to New Jersey, will result in no New Jersey tax of the Company&#8217;s net GILTI income and no utilization of the Company&#8217;s New Jersey NOLs for which the valuation allowance was released in the third quarter of 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, in the fourth quarter of 2018, the Company recorded a full valuation allowance against the New Jersey NOLs. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The domestic valuation allowance for the years ended December 31, 2018, 2017 and 2016 increased $722, $264 and $2,294, respectively.&#160; The 2018, 2017 and 2016 increases in the domestic valuation allowance are due to domestic state items.&#160; </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The foreign valuation allowance for the years ended December 31, 2018, 2017 and 2016 decreased $283, increased $101, and decreased $698, respectively.&#160; The 2018 decrease in the foreign valuation allowance was allocated as follows: the valuation allowance decreased $246 for foreign income and decreased $37 for currency translation adjustments included in other comprehensive income (&#8220;OCI&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2017 increase in the foreign valuation allowance was allocated as follows: the valuation allowance increased $51 for foreign losses and increased $50 for currency translation adjustments included in OCI.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2016 decrease in the foreign valuation allowance was allocated as follows: the valuation allowance decreased $621 for foreign income and decreased $77 for currency translation adjustments included in OCI.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">63</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CAMBREX CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>

<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Due in part to a continuing desire to limit credit and currency exposure for cash held in foreign currencies or in non-U.S. banks, the Company previously determined that it was likely that a portion of the undistributed earnings of its foreign subsidiaries would be repatriated to the U.S. in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under TCJA&#8217;s transition to a modified territorial tax system whereby future repatriations of foreign earnings will generally be exempt from U.S. tax, it is likely that the Company will continue to repatriate certain foreign earnings in the future.&nbsp;&nbsp;Therefore, the Company will continue to monitor available evidence and its plans for foreign earnings and expects to continue to provide any applicable deferred taxes based on the tax liability or withholding taxes that would be due upon repatriation of amounts not considered permanently reinvested.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Gross interest and penalties at December 31, 2018, 2017, and 2016, of $455, $412, and $455, respectively, related to the above unrecognized tax benefits are not reflected in the table above.&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2018, 2017, and 2016, the Company accrued $99, $153, and $63, respectively, of interest and penalties in the income statement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Consistent with prior periods, the Company recognizes interest and penalties within its income tax provision.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Tax years 2012 and forward in the U.S. are open to examination by the IRS.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is also subject to examinations in its material non-U.S. jurisdictions for 2012 and later years.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is also regularly subject to audits in various states for various years.&#160;&#160;<font style="color:#000000;">P</font>revious state audits have resulted in immaterial adjustments.&#160;&#160;In the majority of states where the Company files, the Company is subject to examination for tax years 2013 and forward.</p>

<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">Long&#8209;term Debt</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In May 2016, the Company entered into a $500,000 five-year Syndicated Senior Revolving Credit Facility (&#8220;Credit Facility&#8221;) which expires in May 2021.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company pays interest on this Credit Facility at LIBOR plus 1.25% - 2.00% based upon certain financial measurements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Credit Facility also includes financial covenants regarding interest coverage and leverage ratios. As of December 31, 2018, there was $300,000 outstanding on the Credit Facility. As of December 31, 2017, the facility was undrawn. The 2018 weighted average interest rate for long-term bank debt was 3.8%.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 2, 2019, the Company amended and restated its Credit Facility. <p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">Derivatives and Hedging Activities</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company operates internationally and is exposed to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates and interest rates in the normal course of business.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company, from time to time, uses derivatives to reduce exposure to market risks resulting from fluctuations in interest rates and foreign exchange rates.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">All financial instruments involve market and credit risks.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is exposed to credit losses in the event of non-performance by the counterparties to the contracts.&nbsp;&nbsp;While there can be no assurance, the Company does not anticipate non-performance by these counterparties. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Foreign Currency Forward Contracts </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company periodically enters into foreign currency forward contracts to protect against currency fluctuations of forecasted cash flows and existing balance sheet exposures at its foreign operations, as deemed appropriate.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company may or may not elect to designate certain forward contracts for hedge accounting treatment. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For derivatives that are not designated for hedge accounting treatment, changes in the fair value are immediately recognized in earnings. This treatment has the potential to increase volatility of the Company&#8217;s earnings.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">None of the foreign currency forward contracts entered into during 2018 or 2017 were designated for hedge accounting treatment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The notional amounts of the Company&#8217;s outstanding foreign exchange forward contracts were $35,734, $32,781 and $20,896 at December 31, 2018, 2017, and 2016, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not hold or purchase any foreign currency forward contracts for trading or speculative purposes and no contractual term is greater than twelve months.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The fair value of the Company&#8217;s foreign exchange forward contracts outstanding was a loss of $430 and a gain of $83 at December 31, 2018 and 2017, respectively. Losses are reflected under the caption &#8220;Accrued expenses and other current liabilities&#8221; and a gain is reflected under the caption &#8220;Prepaid expenses and other current assets&#8221; on the Company&#8217;s balance sheet and &#8220;Other revenues, net&#8221; on the Company&#8217;s income statement.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">65</a></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">U.S. GAAP establishes a valuation hierarchy for disclosure of the inputs to the valuations used to measure fair value. This hierarchy prioritizes the inputs into three broad levels as follows: Level 1 inputs are quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities; Level 2 inputs are quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in active markets, quoted prices for identical or similar assets in markets that are not active, inputs other than quoted prices that are observable for the asset or liability, including interest rates, yield curves and credit risks, or inputs that are derived principally from, or corroborated by, observable market data through correlation; Level 3 inputs are unobservable inputs based on the Company&#8217;s assumptions used to measure assets and liabilities at fair value. A financial asset or liability&#8217;s classification within the hierarchy is determined based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;letter-spacing:0pt;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following table provides the assets and liabilities carried at fair value, measured on a recurring basis, as of December 31, 2018 and 2017.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s foreign currency forward contracts are measured at fair value using observable market inputs such as forward rates, the Company&#8217;s credit risk and its counterparties&#8217; credit risks. Based on the Company&#8217;s continued ability to enter into forward contracts, the Company considers the markets for its fair value instruments to be active.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Based on these inputs, the Company&#8217;s foreign currency forward contracts are classified within Level 2 of the valuation hierarchy.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s financial instruments also include cash and cash equivalents, accounts receivables and accounts payables.&nbsp;&nbsp;The carrying amount of these instruments approximates fair value because of their short-term nature.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">During 2018, the Company acquired a 19.9% equity investment in a European company (&#8220;Investee&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;The Investee completed an initial public offering on a foreign exchange late in the second quarter, which reduced the Company&#8217;s ownership share to 16.3%.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#8217;s investment is subject to a prohibition on selling the shares for one year following the acquisition.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has one seat on the Board of Directors of the Investee and concluded it is able to exercise significant influence and that equity accounting would be appropriate.&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with ASC 825, the Company has elected to record this investment at fair value.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company selected an appropriate valuation methodology to compute a discount for the lack of marketability to be applied to the closing market price of the shares as of December&#160;31, 2018. The fair value of the Company&#8217;s shares increased to $13,048 during the year ended December 31, 2018 resulting in an unrealized gain that was recorded as &#8220;Unrealized gain on investment in equity securities&#8221; on the income statement and &#8220;Prepaid expenses and other current assets&#8221; on the balance sheet.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since the shares owned by the Company are substantially in excess of the daily trade volumes of the stock, it could be difficult to sell the shares in a timely manner when the restrictions lapse and it is possible the ultimate value to be realized by the Company could be significantly less upon a sale of the securities.</p>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Refer to Note 13 to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements for further disclosures on the Company&#8217;s financial instruments. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">66</a></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company does not have any publicly traded stock options; therefore, expected volatilities are based on historical volatility of the Company&#8217;s stock.&nbsp;&nbsp;The risk-free interest rate is based on the yield of a zero-coupon U.S. Treasury bond whose maturity period approximates the option&#8217;s expected term.&nbsp;&nbsp;The expected life assumption represents the weighted-average period of time that newly granted stock-based awards are expected to remain outstanding. The expected life is estimated by analyzing three components of historical grants with the same vesting schedules: (i) observed post-vesting forfeiture, (ii) observed exercise behavior, and (iii) expected exercise behavior. The expected time to early exercise is calculated by assuming that the options outstanding as of the valuation date will be exercised at the midpoint between the final vest date and the expiration date. If a grant is already fully vested, it is assumed the outstanding options exercise at the midpoint between the valuation date and the expiration date. The three components are then option-weighted to estimate expected life. The Company stratifies its employees as Board of Directors, Named Executives and all other employees, each group with its own exercise behavior and thus, expected life. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">68</a></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">For 2018, 2017 and 2016, the Company recorded $533, $571 and $489, respectively, in selling, general and administrative expenses for restricted stock units.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2018, there was no compensation cost related to unvested restricted stock not yet recognized.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Domestic Pension Plan</p>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company maintains a defined benefit pension plan (&#8220;Domestic Pension Plan&#8221;) for certain salaried and certain hourly employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is the Company&#8217;s policy to contribute to the domestic pension plan to ensure adequate funds are available in the plan to make benefit payments to plan participants and beneficiaries when required.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also had a Supplemental Executive Retirement Plan (&#8220;SERP&#8221;) for key executives.&nbsp;&nbsp;This plan was non-qualified and unfunded.&nbsp;&nbsp;Benefits accruing under both plans were frozen in 2007.&nbsp;&nbsp;In July 2008, the Board of Directors of the Company amended the SERP to allow for lump sum payments effective January 1, 2009.&nbsp;&nbsp;The lump sum value as of January 1, 2009 was paid in 10 equal actuarial equivalent installments through 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">International Pension Plans</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A foreign subsidiary of the Company maintains a pension plan (&#8220;International Pension Plan&#8221;) for its employees that conforms to the common practice in that country.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on local laws and customs, this plan is unfunded.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

Services costs are recognized in &#8220;Selling, general and administrative expenses&#8221; and &#8220;Cost of goods sold&#8221; in its income statement depending on the functional area of the underlying employees included in the plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result of the adoption of ASU 2017-07, the Company recorded $813 for the year ended December 31, 2018 to &#8220;Other expenses, net&#8221; which formerly would have been recorded as &#8220;Selling, general and administrative expenses&#8221; or &#8220;Cost of goods sold.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;To conform to the current year presentation, for the years ended December 31, 2017 and 2016, the Company reclassified $1,484 and $1,540, respectively, from &#8220;Selling, general and administrative expenses&#8221; and $216 and $163, respectively, from &#8220;Cost of goods sold&#8221; to &#8220;Other expenses, net.&#8221;</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In making its assumption for the long-term rate of return on plan assets, the Company has utilized historical rates earned on securities allocated consistently with its investments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The discount rate was selected by projecting cash flows associated with plan obligations, which were matched to a yield curve of high quality corporate bonds.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company then selected the single rate that produced the same present value as if each cash flow were discounted by the corresponding spot rate on the yield curve. </p>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The aggregate Accumulated Benefit Obligation (&#8220;ABO&#8221;) of $53,421 exceeds plan assets by $12,880 as of December 31, 2018 for the Domestic Pension Plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;The aggregate ABO is $28,982 for the International Pension Plan as of December 31, 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;The International Pension Plan is unfunded.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company expects to contribute approximately $255 in cash to the Domestic Pension Plan in 2019.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not expect to contribute cash to its International Pension Plan in 2019.</p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Savings Plan</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cambrex makes available to all domestic employees a savings plan. Employee contributions are matched in part by Cambrex.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cost of this plan amounted to $1,745, $1,491 and $1,294 in 2018, 2017 and 2016, respectively.</p>
<div align="left">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:4.79%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(1</font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">9</font><font style="font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">)</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;font-weight:bold;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">Segment Information</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Cambrex is a life sciences company that provides products and services that accelerate and improve the development and commercialization of new and generic therapeutics.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company primarily supplies its products and services worldwide to innovator and generic pharmaceutical companies.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">73</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CAMBREX CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(dollars in thousands, except share and per share data)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU71"></a><font style="font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Including the Company&#8217;s acquisition of Halo Pharma on September 12, 2018, </font><font style="font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">which represents the Finished Dosage Form (&#8220;FDF&#8221;) segment, </font><font style="letter-spacing:0pt;">Cambrex has six manufacturing facilities.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;color:#000000;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Operating segments are identified as components of an enterprise for which separate discrete financial information is available for evaluation by the chief operating decision maker (the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer) in making decisions on how to allocate resources and assess performance. To be in alignment with the financial information received by the Chief Executive Officer and how the business is managed, the Company&#8217;s five operating segments were aggregated to form two reportable segments, <font style="letter-spacing:0pt;color:#000000;">A</font><font style="color:#000000;">ctive Pharmaceutical Ingredients (&#8220;APIs&#8221;) </font><font style="letter-spacing:0pt;color:#000000;">and FDF.</font><font style="color:#000000;">&#160;&#160;</font>All purchase accounting adjustments are recorded by the reporting segment.</p>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="text-decoration:underline;">API&#8217;s:</font> <font style="font-style:normal;">The Company&#8217;s API segment is comprised of the custom development and manufacture of pharmaceutical ingredients derived from organic chemistry.&nbsp;&nbsp;APIs are used in the production of prescription and over-the-counter drug products.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="text-decoration:underline;">FDF:</font>&nbsp;&nbsp;<font style="font-style:normal;">The Company&#8217;s FDF segment consists of contract development and commercial manufacturing of finished dosage form products including oral solids, liquids and creams, and sterile and non-sterile ointments.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:11pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company&#8217;s Corporate headquarters provides management and administrative services to support the Company, and consists of certain aspects of the Company&#8217;s executive management, legal, compliance, human resources, information technology and finance departments. The Company allocates certain corporate expenses to each of its segments. Depreciation and amortization on certain assets are not allocated to the Company&#8217;s reportable segments.</p>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company evaluates the performance of its segments based on segment operating profit. Transactions between reportable segments are not material.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company does not allocate interest expense or income taxes to the operating segments.&nbsp;&nbsp;Discontinued operations are not recorded by the reportable segments. The Company accounts for total assets on a consolidated basis and does not allocate or disclose it for each reportable segment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The chief operating decision maker does not review segment&#8217;s assets.</p>
<p style="margin-top:11pt;text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The following table summarizes the Company&#8217;s financial information by reportable segment: </p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;font-weight:bold;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:11pt;">Contingencies</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is subject to various investigations, claims and legal proceedings covering a wide range of matters that arise in the ordinary course of its business activities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company continually assesses known facts and circumstances as they pertain to applicable legal and environmental matters and evaluates the need for reserves and disclosures as deemed necessary based on these facts and circumstances.&nbsp;&nbsp;These matters, either individually or in the aggregate, could result in actual costs that are significantly higher than the Company&#8217;s current assessment and could have a material adverse effect on the Company's operating results and cash flows in future reporting periods. Based upon past experience, the Company believes that payments significantly in excess of current reserves, if required, would be made over an extended number of years.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Environmental</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In connection with laws and regulations pertaining to the protection of the environment, the Company and its subsidiaries are a party to several environmental proceedings and remediation activities and along with other companies, have been named a potentially responsible party (&#8220;PRP&#8221;) for certain waste disposal sites ("Superfund sites").&nbsp;&nbsp;All of the liabilities currently recorded on the Company&#8217;s balance sheet for environmental proceedings are associated with discontinued operations. The Company had insurance policies in place at certain of the discontinued operations for certain years that the Company believes should cover some portion of the recorded liabilities or potential future liabilities and the Company expects the net cash impact related to the contingencies described below to be reduced by the applicable income tax rate.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">It is the Company&#8217;s policy to record appropriate liabilities for environmental matters where remedial efforts are probable and the costs can be reasonably estimated.&nbsp;&nbsp;Such liabilities are based on the Company&#8217;s estimate of the undiscounted future costs required to complete the remedial work.&nbsp;&nbsp;Each of these matters is subject to various uncertainties, and it is possible that some of these matters will be decided against the Company. The resolution of such matters often spans several years and frequently involves regulatory oversight or adjudication.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, many remediation requirements are fluid and are likely to be affected by future technological, site and regulatory developments.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is not possible at this time for the Company to determine fully the effect of all asserted and unasserted claims on its consolidated financial condition, results of operations or liquidity; however, to the extent possible, where asserted and unasserted claims can be estimated and where such claims are considered probable, the Company would record a liability. Consequently, the ultimate liability with respect to such matters, as well as the timing of cash disbursements, is uncertain.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">76</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CAMBREX CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(dollars in thousands, except share and per share data)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU74"></a><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In matters w</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">here the Company is able to reasonably estimate the probable and estimable costs associated with environmental proceedings, the Company accrues for the estimated costs associated with the study and remediation of applicable sites. At December 31, 2018, the</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">se reserves were $</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">17,411</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, of which $</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">16,599</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> is included in &#8220;Other non-current liabilities&#8221; on the Company&#8217;s balance sheet. At December 31, 2017, the reserves were $17,511, of which $16,976 is included in &#8220;Other non-current liabilities&#8221; on the Company&#8217;s bala</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">nce sheet. The increase in the reserves includes adjustments to reserves of $</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">1,055</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, partially offset by payments of $</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">1,155</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">. The reserves are adjusted periodically as remediation efforts progress or as additional technical, regulatory or legal information b</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ecomes available.&nbsp;&nbsp;Given the uncertainties regarding the outcome of investigative and study activities, the status of laws, regulations, enforcement, policies, the impact of other PRPs, technology and information related to individual sites, the Company do</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">es not believe it is possible to currently develop an estimate of the range of reasonably possible environmental loss in excess of its reserves.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Bayonne </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As a result of the sale of a Bayonne, New Jersey facility, the Company became obligated to investigate site conditions and conduct required remediation under the New Jersey Industrial Site Recovery Act.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is completing an investigation and sampling plan at the property pursuant to the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection&#8217;s (&#8220;NJDEP&#8221;) private oversight program.&nbsp;&nbsp;The results will be used to develop a proposed remedial action work plan for the site.&nbsp;&nbsp;Among other things, the remedial plan is anticipated to set forth further details of the proposed cleanup, including the removal and/or encapsulation of certain impacted soils and implementation of engineering controls and deed restrictions.  As of December 31, 2018, the Company&#8217;s reserve was $608.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Clifton and Carlstadt</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has implemented a sampling and pilot program in Clifton and Carlstadt, New Jersey pursuant to the NJDEP private oversight program.&nbsp;&nbsp;The results of the sampling and pilot program to date have been used to develop an estimate of the Company's future liability for remediation costs, and the Company continues to move forward with the projects at each site in accordance with the established schedules and work plans.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2018, the Company&#8217;s reserve was $1,827.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Berry&#8217;s Creek</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company received a notice from the United States Environmental Protection Agency (&#8220;USEPA&#8221;) that two subsidiaries of the Company are considered PRPs at the Berry&#8217;s Creek Study Area in New Jersey.&nbsp;&nbsp;These subsidiaries are among many other PRPs that were listed in the notice.&#160; Pursuant to the notice, the PRPs have been asked to perform a remedial investigation (&#8220;RI&#8221;) and feasibility study (&#8220;FS&#8221;) of the Berry&#8217;s Creek site. The Company has joined the group of PRPs and entered into an Administrative Settlement Agreement (&#8220;Agreement&#8221;) and Order on Consent with the USEPA agreeing to jointly conduct or fund an appropriate remedial investigation and feasibility study of the Berry&#8217;s Creek site with the other PRPs in the Agreement. The PRPs have engaged consultants to perform the work specified in the Agreement and develop a method to allocate related costs among the PRPs.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In June 2016, the PRPs received a request from USEPA to amend the RI/FS Work Plan to accommodate a phased, iterative approach to the Berry&#8217;s Creek remediation.&nbsp;&nbsp;USEPA requested an initial Phase I remedy that focuses on a portion of the site, namely, sediments in Upper and Middle Berry&#8217;s Creek and the marsh in Upper Peach Island Creek.&nbsp;&nbsp;Any subsequent remedial action will occur after the implementation and performance monitoring of this Phase I remedy and the extent of future action is expected to be at least partially determined by the outcome of this initial phase.&nbsp;&nbsp;In April 2017, USEPA approved the requested addendum to the RI/FS Work Plan, which included the description of the phased and adaptive management approach to the Berry&#8217;s Creek remedy.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">77</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CAMBREX CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(dollars in thousands, except share and per share data)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU75"></a><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In September 2018, USEPA issued its Record of Decision (&#8220;ROD&#8221;) for an interim remedy at Berry&#8217;s Creek.&nbsp;&nbsp;The interim remedy calls for, among other things, dredging and capping of contaminated sediments.&nbsp;&nbsp;The next step in the process is to d</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">esign the remedy (&#8220;Remedial Design&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;USEPA issued a letter to the Berry&#8217;s Creek PRP Group in September 2018 that provided notice of potential liability and a request that the PRP Group agree to perform the Remedial Design.&nbsp;&nbsp;USEPA provided a draft settlem</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ent agreement and statement of work to implement the Remedial Design.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a member of the Berry&#8217;s Creek PRP Group, the Company will participate in the PRP Group&#8217;s </font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">engagement with </font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">USEPA</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> on Remedial Design</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">, and is coordinating with PRP Group members and PRP </font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Group</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> common counsel accordingly</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The estimated costs for the interim remedy may be further developed and the Company&#8217;s accrual may change based upon revisions to cost estimates. As of December 31, 2018, the Company&#8217;s reserve was $9,647.&nbsp;&nbsp;At this time it is not known when the costs for the complete remediation plan will be estimable, and as such, no accrual beyond the interim remedy has been recorded. The Company&#8217;s share has been preliminarily estimated by the PRP group at 2.4%. While the Company will defend its position that its share should be reduced from the current level, its share could be increased or decreased depending on the outcome of the final allocation process that will take place in future periods.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">While any resolution of this matter is not expected to materially impact the Company&#8217;s operations or financial position, it could be material to the financial statements in the period recorded.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In July 2014, the Company received a notice from the U.S. Department of the Interior, U.S. Fish &amp; Wildlife Service, regarding the Company&#8217;s potential liability for natural resource damages at the Berry&#8217;s Creek site and inviting the Company to participate in a cooperative assessment of natural resource damages.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most members of the Berry&#8217;s Creek PRP group received such notice letters, and the PRP Group coordinated a joint response, which was to decline participation in a cooperative assessment at this time, given existing investigation work at the site.&nbsp;&nbsp;The cost of any future assessment and the ultimate scope of natural resource damage liability are not yet known.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Maybrook Site</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A subsidiary of Cambrex is named a PRP of a site in Hamptonburgh, New York by the USEPA in connection with the discharge, under appropriate permits, of wastewater at that site prior to Cambrex's acquisition in 1986.&nbsp;&nbsp;The PRPs implemented soil remediation which was completed in 2012 pending approval by the USEPA.&nbsp;&nbsp;The PRPs will continue implementing the ground water remediation at the site.&nbsp;&nbsp;USEPA completed its 5-year review report in August 2018, and USEPA&#8217;s review of the site remedy is on-going.&nbsp;&nbsp;It is unclear if such review, together with an agreed proposed modification to the USEPA Consent Decree, will result in any additional site work.&nbsp;&nbsp;In November 2018, under a statewide initiative, the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (&#8220;NYSDEC&#8221;) requested that the PRPs perform additional sampling for certain &#8220;emerging contaminants.&#8221;&nbsp;&nbsp;NYSDEC approved the PRPs work plan in December 2018, and the sampling is anticipated to be performed during the first quarter of 2019.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2018, the Company&#8217;s reserve was $329, to cover long-term ground water monitoring and related costs.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Harriman Site</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Subsidiaries of Cambrex and Pfizer are named as responsible parties for the Company&#8217;s former Harriman, New York production facility by the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (&#8220;NYSDEC&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;A final Record of Decision (&#8220;ROD&#8221;) describing the Harriman site remediation responsibilities for Pfizer and the Company was issued in 1997 (the &#8220;1997 ROD&#8221;) and incorporated into a federal court Consent Decree in 1998 (the &#8220;Consent Decree&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;In December 2013, the Company, Pfizer and the NYSDEC entered into a federal court stipulation, which the court subsequently endorsed as a court order, resolving certain disputes with the NYSDEC about the scope of the obligations under the Consent Decree and the 1997 ROD, and requiring the Company and Pfizer to carry out an environmental investigation and study of certain areas of the Harriman Site. </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">78</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CAMBREX CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(dollars in thousands, except share and per share data)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU76"></a><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Site clean-up work under the 1997 ROD, the Consent Decree and the 2013 stipulation is ongoing and is being jointly performed by Pfizer and the Company, with NYSDEC oversight.&nbsp;&nbsp;Since 2014, Pfizer and the Com</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">pany have performed supplemental remedial investigation measures requested by the NYSDEC, and the findings have been submitted to NYSDEC in various reports, including a study evaluating the feasibility of certain remedial alternatives in August 2016.&nbsp;&nbsp;By l</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">etter dated January 5, 2017, NYSDEC disapproved such feasibility study report and requested certain revisions to the report.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company and Pfizer engaged in further discussions with NYSDEC and have agreed to submit a revised version of the August 2016 f</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">easibility study to address certain of NYSDEC&#8217;s requests.&nbsp;&nbsp;In September 2017, the NYSDEC requested that Pfizer, the Company and the current owner of the Harriman Site, ELT Harriman LLC (&#8220;ELT&#8221;), conduct an investigation of additional constituents not addres</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">sed under the 1997 ROD based on the detection of those constituents at the Harriman Site and other properties in the area.&nbsp;&nbsp;The parties have requested more information from the State of New York to evaluate the request, while also responding to NYSDEC that</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> no further investigation was warranted.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As it is too soon to determine whether the NYSDEC&#8217;s requests or the reports and remedial plans, when finalized, will result in any significant changes to the Company&#8217;s responsibilities, no change to the reserve has been made. ELT is conducting other investigation and remediation activities under a separate NYSDEC directive.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">No final remedy for the site has been determined, which will follow further discussions with the NYSDEC.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company estimates the range for its share of the liability at the site to be between $2,000 and $7,000.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2018, the Company&#8217;s reserve was $3,365.&nbsp;&nbsp;At this time, the Company is unable to provide an estimate of the ultimate investigative and remedial costs to the Company for any final remedy selected by the NYSDEC.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company intends to enforce all of its contractual rights to recover costs and for indemnification under a 2007 settlement agreement, and has filed such claims in an arbitration proceeding against ELT and the immediately preceding owner, Vertellus Specialties Holdings (&#8220;Vertellus&#8221;). ELT has filed counterclaims, and has threatened to file additional counterclaims, for contractual indemnification and for breach of the settlement agreement against the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;Currently, the arbitration proceeding is stayed indefinitely.&nbsp;&nbsp;In May 2016, some but not all of the Vertellus entities who are parties to the Company&#8217;s 2007 settlement agreement filed for restructuring under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has filed several claims as creditors in the bankruptcy proceeding and will continue to monitor the bankruptcy proceeding.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Scientific Chemical Processing (&#8220;SCP&#8221;) Superfund Site</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">A subsidiary of Cambrex was named a PRP of the SCP Superfund site, located in Carlstadt, New Jersey, along with approximately 130 other PRPs.&nbsp;&nbsp;The site is a former waste processing facility that accepted various waste for recovery and disposal including processing wastewater from this subsidiary.&nbsp;&nbsp;The PRPs are in the process of implementing a final remedy at the site.&nbsp;&nbsp;The SCP Superfund site has also been identified as a PRP in the Berry&#8217;s Creek Superfund site (see previous discussion). While the Company continues to dispute the methodology used by the PRP group to arrive at its interim allocation for cash contributions, the Company has paid the funding requests.&nbsp;&nbsp;A final allocation of SCP Site costs (excluding Berry&#8217;s Creek costs) is expected to be finalized in 2019.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2018, the Company&#8217;s reserve was $732, of which approximately $468 is expected to be covered by insurance. </p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Newark Bay Complex</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The USEPA and a private party group are evaluating remediation plans for the Passaic River, Newark Bay, Hackensack River, Arthur Kill, Kill Van Kull and adjacent waters (the &#8220;Newark Bay Complex&#8221;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Although the Company is not involved in the USEPA action, it continues to monitor developments related to the site due to its past involvement in a previously settled state action relating to the Newark Bay Complex.&nbsp;&nbsp;The USEPA has finalized its decision on a cleanup plan for 8.3 miles of the lower Passaic River, and has estimated the cost of this plan at $1.38 billion.&nbsp;&nbsp;Due to the uncertainty of the future scope and timing of any possible claims against the Company, no liability has been recorded.&nbsp;&nbsp; </p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">79</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">CAMBREX CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">(dollars in thousands, except share and per share data)</p>
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU77"></a><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company is involved in other related and unrelated environmental matters where the range of liability is not reasonably estimable at this time and it is not fo</font><font style="font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">reseeable when information will become available to provide a basis for adjusting or recording a reserve, should a reserve ultimately be required.</font><font style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;</font></p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:4.79%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Other</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company has commitments incident to the ordinary course of business including corporate guarantees of certain subsidiary obligations to the Company&#8217;s lenders related to financial assurance obligations under certain environmental laws for remediation; closure and third party liability requirements of certain of its subsidiaries and a former operating location; contract provisions for indemnification protecting its customers and suppliers against third party liability for the manufacture and sale of Company products that fail to meet product warranties and contract provisions for indemnification protecting licensees against intellectual property infringement related to licensed Company technology or processes.</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Additionally, as permitted under Delaware law, the Company indemnifies its officers, directors and employees for certain events or occurrences while the officer, director or employee is, or was, serving at the Company&#8217;s request in such capacity. The term of the indemnification period is for the officer's, director's or employee&#8217;s lifetime. The maximum potential amount of future payments the Company could be required to make under these indemnification agreements is unlimited; however, the Company has a director and officer insurance policy that covers a portion of any potential exposure.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company currently believes the estimated fair value of its indemnification agreements is not material based on currently available information, and as such, the Company had no liabilities recorded for these agreements as of December 31, 2018.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-top:11pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The Company's subsidiaries are party to a number of other proceedings that are not considered material at this time.<font style="font-weight:bold;"> </font></p>

<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;;font-size:11pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:justify;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:4.79%;font-size:11pt;letter-spacing:-0.15pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">On January 2, 2019, the Company completed the acquisition of 100% of Avista Pharma Solutions, a contract development, manufacturing, and testing organization with sites located in Durham, NC, Longmont, CO, Agawam, MA and Edinburgh, Scotland, UK.&nbsp;&nbsp;The purchase price of approximately $252,000 was funded with a combination of cash on hand and borrowings under a new senior secured credit facility, following a refinancing completed on the same day.&nbsp;&nbsp;The amended and restated Credit Facility is a $800,000 five-year Syndicated Senior Credit Facility expiring January 2, 2024, comprising of a $600,000 Revolving Credit Facility and $200,000 Term Loan A.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company pays interest on the New Credit Facility at LIBOR plus 1.25% - 2.00% based upon certain financial measurements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The New Credit Facility also includes financial covenants regarding interest coverage and leverage ratios.</p>
